### Public Procurement Manual
(Second Edition – 2020)

The Public Procurement Manual (Second Edition – 2020) serves as a comprehensive guide to the public procurement processes in Sierra Leone. Developed by the National Public Procurement Authority (NPPA), the manual outlines the legal framework, procedures, and best practices for efficient, transparent, and accountable procurement across all public institutions. It is an essential reference for procurement officers, suppliers, contractors, and stakeholders involved in public sector procurement.

### Application and Limitations of Manual

This Manual applies to the procurement operations of all institutions using public funds as defined in Subsection 1 of Section 1 of the Public Procurement Act 2016. Home / News & Notices / Sierra Leone Moves Resident and Work Permit Applications Fully Online

# Sierra Leone Moves Resident and Work Permit Applications Fully Online

Non-citizens in Sierra Leone must now apply for and renew resident and work permits through a new online platform as government ends manual processing.

Sierra Leone has officially launched a fully digital system for resident and work permit processing, marking a major shift in how immigration-related services are handled for non-citizens living and working in the country. The change took effect on January 1, 2026, with government notices stating that applications and renewals are now expected to go through the online permits platform rather than the previous manual process.

The move is being presented as part of a broader modernization effort aimed at improving efficiency, transparency, and service delivery within the country’s immigration framework. For employers, foreign workers, and long-term residents, the new system is expected to reduce paperwork bottlenecks and create a more centralized record of permit activity.

The reform is significant because immigration permit processing often affects investment, labor mobility, and regulatory compliance. By shifting the process online, Sierra Leone is signaling a more structured and technology-driven approach to managing residence and work authorization.

For applicants, the message is straightforward: the digital route is now the main channel, and anyone seeking to renew or obtain a resident or work permit should prepare to use the online platform going forward
